chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, all together, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (عليه السلام) saying: 'O Thabit, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, had appointed a time for this matter in the year seventy. Then, when al-Husayn, may the blessings of Allah be upon him, was killed, the wrath of Allah, Exalted is He, intensified against the people of the earth, so He delayed it until one hundred and forty.'
Then we narrated it to you, but you spread the hadith, and so you uncovered the covering of concealment; and after that Allah did not set any time for it with us.
And Allah effaces whatever He wills and confirms, and with Him is the Mother of the Book.
Abu Hamza said: 'So I related that to Abu Abdillah (عليه السلام), and he said: It had indeed been so.'

key_terms.أُمُّ الْكِتَابِ: the Mother of the Book; the foundational source of decree with Allah
key_terms.هَذَا الْأَمْرَ: this matter; the divinely ordained affair referred to in the narration

ai.seo_question: Why do Shia hadith say the time of the Imam’s re-appearance was changed or withheld?
ai.summary: This hadith states that a time had been appointed for this matter, but it was delayed after the killing of al-Husayn (عليه السلام), and later no specific time remained disclosed. It emphasizes that divine decree may be altered in what is disclosed to creation, while ultimate knowledge remains with Allah. The report also warns against publicizing restricted teachings concerning the timing of eschatological events.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad and Muhammad Bin Al Hassan, from Sahl Bin Ziyad and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, altogether, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Abu Hamza Al Sumaly who said,

‘I heard Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘O Sabit! Allah<sup>asws</sup> Blessed and High has (Fixed) a time for this matter in (the year) seventy (A.H.). So when Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> was killed, the Wrath of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Intensified upon the people of the earth, therefore He<sup>azwj</sup> Delayed it to (the year) one hundred and forty (A.H.).

So we<sup>asws</sup> narrated it to you all, but you broadcast the Hadeeth, and so you uncovered the covering of the veil; and Allah<sup>azwj</sup> did not Make a (specific) time for it after that with us<sup>asws</sup>.
[13:39] Allah Obliterates whatever He so Desires to and Establishes, and with Him is the Mother of the Book

’.
Abu Hamza said, ‘So I narrated with that to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It has been like that’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Hassan have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa all from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from abu Hamza al-Thumali who has said the following.

“I heard abu Ja’far (a.s.) say, “O Thabit, Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, had set up a time limit for it in the year seventy but when al-Husayn (a.s.) was murdered Allah’s anger became more intense on the people on earth. He delayed it until one hundred forty.
When then spoke to you about it and you publicized this hadith and disclosed the secret.
Allah thereafter has not set up a time limit for it available with us. Allah deletes whatever He wants and establishes whatever He wants, with Him is the original book.
Abu Hamza has said, “I narrated the above Hadith to abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) and he said, “It was as you said.”
